goal_summary: Bounded source investigation and primary-literature curation of five IMA-approved single-reference critical-element mineral species with open-access type descriptions in European Journal of Mineralogy (volumes 36, 37, and 38): heimaeyite (IMA:2023-127a, Na3Al(SO4)3), delchiaroite (IMA:2025-076, symbol Dch, Cu3I(CH3S)2), marioantofilliite (IMA:2025-012, symbol Maf, [Cu4Al2(OH)12](CO3)(H2O)3), jonlarsenite (IMA:2024-078a, Al4Cu9), and nannoniite (IMA:2024-010, symbol Nnn, Al2(OH)5F). Direct inspection of IMA_Master_List_(2026-09).pdf (pages 55, 91, 106, 136, 151) and bounded per-page passage indexing (170 passages <= 1,799 B across 61 full-PDF pages) plus 28 single-page 150-DPI PNG table renders verified all chemical, crystallographic, optical, and locality claims and identified the remaining uncurated EJM frontier queue.

primary_source.citation: Balic-Zunic T, Garavelli A, Mitolo D, Nestola F, Pamato MG, Rasmussen MB, Jolnaes MB (2025) Heimaeyite, Na3Al(SO4)3, a new mineral from the fumaroles on Eldfell volcano, Iceland. European Journal of Mineralogy 37:79-89

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 80) JEOL JXA-8200 WDS EMPA chemistry (n = 11 analyses: mean Fe2O3 4.18 wt% [SD 0.58], MnO 0.43 wt% [SD 0.16], K2O 0.98 wt% [SD 0.14], SO3 56.72 wt% [SD 1.40], SiO2 0.10 wt% [SD 0.07], Al2O3 10.10 wt% [SD 0.57], MgO 1.00 wt% [SD 0.12], Na2O 19.39 wt% [SD 0.79], printed Total 92.89 wt% [exact sum of rounded means 92.90 wt%]; empirical formula after subtracting admixed koryakite and EA: Na2.93Al0.82Fe0.25S2.99O12.05; SCXRD refined formula Na3Al0.93Fe0.07S3O12)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Three different calculated density values appear across the primary paper: 2.783 g cm-3 in the Abstract (p. 79) and Section 2 (p. 80, from empirical chemical analysis and SCXRD unit-cell dimensions), 2.747 g cm-3 in Section 2 (p. 80, from crystal structure analysis results), and 2.7411 in Table 3 (p. 84, where the row header prints a typographical unit error 'Calculated density (g cm-1)' instead of 'g cm-3').
Table 1 (p. 80) prints Total = 92.89 wt%, whereas the exact arithmetic sum of the eight rounded mean wt% values (4.18 + 0.43 + 0.98 + 56.72 + 0.10 + 10.10 + 1.00 + 19.39) is 92.90 wt%.
The Abstract (p. 79) describes the streak of natural Fe-bearing heimaeyite as 'yellowish streak', whereas Section 2 (p. 80) states 'The streak is yellow' (and white for pure synthetic Na3Al(SO4)3).

Section 4.1 (p. 81) reports multiphase PXRD weight fractions of 41 wt% heimaeyite, 18 wt% tamarugite, 15 wt% koryakite, 11 wt% langbeinite, 9 wt% EA, and 7 wt% hexahydrite, whose rounded integer values sum to 101 wt%.
Section 6 (p. 87) prints the reagent aluminium sulfate hydrate formula as 'Al3(SO4)2(H2O)17' (transposing the Al and SO4 subscripts of Al2(SO4)3*17H2O).

Table 2 (p. 82) footnote states '* The intensities of the eight strongest maxima are in bold', whereas only seven Imeas values (40, 17, 32, 100, 55, 10 at 2.72 A, and 11) are typeset in bold and the tied eighth at 2.026 A (Imeas = 10) is typeset in regular font.

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 737) Cameca SX 100 WDS EMPA chemistry (n = 20 spot analyses: mean SO3 0.07 wt% [esd 0.04, norm 0.07], CO2calc 6.06 wt% [norm 5.74], SiO2 0.54 wt% [esd 0.40, norm 0.51], Al2O3 14.97 wt% [esd 0.51, norm 14.19], MgO 0.12 wt% [esd 0.12, norm 0.11], CuO 56.21 wt% [esd 1.93, norm 53.26], H2Ocalc 27.56 wt% [norm 26.12], unnormalized Total 105.53 wt%, normalized Total 100.00 wt%; empirical formula [Cu2+4.23Mg0.02Al1.76(OH)12](CO3)0.82(SO4)0.01[Si(OH)6]0.05*3H2O on (Cu + Mg + Al) = 6 apfu)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The September 2026 IMA Master List (PDF p. 136) writes the formula as [Cu4Al2(OH)12](CO3)(H2O)3, whereas Biagioni et al. (2025) write [Cu4Al2(OH)12](CO3)*3H2O.

Section 7.4 (p. 741) prints the 6-cation recalculation 'with rounding errors' as [(Cu3.72Al2.28)(OH)12](CO3)1.10*3.06H2O, whereas 6 x [(Cu0.613Al0.387)(OH)2](CO3)0.194*0.486H2O equals [(Cu3.68Al2.32)(OH)12](CO3)1.16*2.92H2O.
Section 7.2 and Table 5 (p. 740) report the interlayer carbonate C-O(1i) distance as 1.28(6) A, whereas Section 7.3 (p. 741) prints 1.28(2) A.

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 1013) Cameca SX 100 WDS EMPA chemistry (n = 9 spots: mean SO3 0.49 wt% [SD 0.14], Al2O3 63.97 wt% [SD 0.46], MgO 0.51 wt% [SD 0.04], CaO 0.22 wt% [SD 0.03], K2O 0.07 wt% [SD 0.02], F 11.72 wt% [SD 0.41], stoichiometric H2O(calc) 28.54 wt%, -O = F -4.94 wt%, Total 100.58 wt%; empirical formula (Al1.99Mg0.02)sum=2.01(SO4)0.01(OH)5.02F0.98 on (OH + F) = 6 apfu; TEM-EDS empirical formula Al2(OH)4.72F1.28)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Under shortwave UV radiation (lambda = 254 nm), the Abstract (p. 1011) describes the fluorescence of nannoniite as 'bluish-yellow', whereas Section 2 (pp. 1012-1013) and Section 4.4.2 (p. 1020) describe it as 'bluish-white' (matching Jambor et al., 1990 for UM1990-28-OHF:Al).

Three sets of monoclinic unit-cell parameters are reported across the study: 3DED (PETS2, Table 3, p. 1016) a = 8.688(3), b = 5.024(2), c = 9.734(4) A, beta = 90.77(2) deg, V = 424.9(3) A3 (rounded in Table 8, p. 1019, to 8.69, 5.02, 9.73 A, 90.8 deg, 424.9 A3); Gandolfi-like PXRD (Section 3.3, p. 1013) a = 8.680(3), b = 5.018(4), c = 9.711(4) A, beta = 90.26(9) deg, V = 423.0(4) A3; and weak SCXRD (Section 3.3, p. 1013) a = 8.672(7), b = 5.009(4), c = 9.673(8) A, beta = 90.50(3) deg, V = 420.2(6) A3.

Section 4.5 (p. 1020) prints the formula of associated dacostaite (IMA 2024-015) as K(Mg2Al)[Mg(H2O)6](AsO4)2F6*2H2O, omitting the subscript 2 on [Mg(H2O)6]2 relative to its charge-balanced ideal formula K(Mg2Al)[Mg(H2O)6]2(AsO4)2F6*2H2O.
